context: a letter from A. Y. Spearman, which you are answering
exchanges: Having laid before the Lords &c your Letter of the 16 Inst inclosing the Account of Messrs Smith & Elder for the first part of the Work entitled The Zoology of the Voyage of H.M.S. Beagle, which is now published, amounting to the sum of £68.10.10. I am commanded by their Ldps to acquaint you that this payt. will be made to Messrs. Smith and Elder at any time by Mr. Sargent, at this Office, on their Application; and that payment will in like manner be ordered to be made hereafter on the receipt of a Certificate from you of the Sum required to be paid, accompanied by a document of the same nature as that now transmitted.— 23d Feb. 1838 A Y Spearman

In pursuance of your directions in your letter of Feby. 23d. 1838, and in accordance with the plan of expenditure, which met (Octbr. 11th. 1837) the approval of the Lords Comm: of Her Majesty’s Treasury, I enclose the accounts for Noo 1 of Part II and Noo 1 of Part III, of the “Zoology of the Voyage of the Beagle”, which have both been published.— I beg leave to state, that as on the former occasion, I have superintended every expense, & the terms agreed on with the artists. I presume, if the account meets with their Lordships approval, Mrrs. Smith and Elder may as before, wait on Mr Sarjent at the Treasury Chambers for payment.

I have the honor to remain | Sir | Your obedient and obliged servant | Charles Darwin To | A. Y. Spearman Esqr

Treasury Chambers.
